subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 32, male. I've been having a lot of pain in both of my elbows, especially the right one. It's been going on for about a year and a half, and it really hurts when I use my arms or hands a lot. I've been taking ibuprofen, but it hasn't helped much. Doctor: Can you describe the nature of the pain in your elbows (e.g., sharp, dull, throbbing)? Doctor: Have you undergone any previous imaging or consultations for this elbow pain? If so, please provide details. Patient: No, I haven't had any imaging or consultations for this before. This is the first time I'm really seeing a doctor about it. I just kept taking ibuprofen and hoping it would get better, but it hasn't. Doctor: Have you experienced any repetitive strain or occupational activities that involve repetitive elbow movements, such as weightlifting, typing, or manual labor? Additionally, do you have a family history of joint or autoimmune conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis? Patient: I lift a lot of weights, like pretty heavy ones, and I've been doing that for a while. I don't think there's any family history of joint issues or arthritis that I'm aware of. Doctor: Have you experienced any stiffness, clicking, or locking in your elbows, and if so, how often does this occur? Patient: No,
